notes:
I opened every listed mock-up shot (brand 8, clarity 6, feel 5 of 8: the three feel loader and v1 shots were not reviewed). I also read the owner's verbatim sections from 1 Nov to 4 Nov and checked each proposal against LK32, LK47 and LK67-LK75.

- **Brand wins on fidelity.** It keeps his approved hero sentence and adds the missing 'what we are' line. It makes Mobi one consistent character with real parity, and its Night reads calm in the shot. Its main fidelity defects are visible or implied: the missing logo dot, the missing hero links, and spotlight and Reveal reductions that should be converted rather than cut.
- **Clarity is a close second.** It has the clearest first glance, but it replaces approved copy and cuts two animations.
- **Feel keeps the tap toy (sheet fill per tap).** Its desktop composition covers the painted sheet, and it changes approved copy.

All three reverse the 1 Nov static-H1 ruling in favour of LK74's typing. Newer words win, but record his agreement. All three also conflict with L-043's 3 s opening, and the final spec should put that length to him as one constant.

notes: I opened every listed shot: 8 for brand, 6 for clarity and 8 for feel. On this lens all three remove the neon cluster, and all three move Night to the app's warm charcoal, which visibly fixes LK68 in every Night shot. The difference is ownership. Brand is the only proposal that makes Mobi one consistent character with jobs, gives questions their own reading voice (Literata), and keeps the approved sentence. Its biggest concrete defect is the missing logo volt dot in its mock-up (confirmed against src/components/Logo.jsx:18-53, which draws the dot by the owner's 15 Oct request). That defect is cheap to fix but must be locked by a test. Clarity is the most legible but the most template-like. Feel has the calmest system thinking but the least character in the shots, and its desktop card sits over the owned art. None of the mock-ups proves motion, real-device scroll or performance; they are static frames.

scores.strengths: Its hero geometry is the most robust of the three. I measured it in its own mock-up: the widest typed phrase, 'second guesses.', is 313 px at 41 px. That fits the 350 px column at 390 and the 320 px column at 360, with document width equal to the viewport at both, so there is no sideways scroll. It has the lowest loader exposure: first visit only with a 30-day memory, any pointer, touch, wheel or key skips it, and hash and same-origin entries skip it too. So the curtain almost never stands between a student and the key. It has the strongest idle performance lever: the rig loops only during an act or glance, and otherwise shows the static poster plus one CSS breath on the compositor, for 0 rAF per second at idle. The statement becomes one 3-step story at both widths, a single code path, which is easier to gate than a split between phone and desktop. It gives six packets with model assignments and an explicit merge order (tokens, then hero, loader, exam and scroll, then page.js assembly). The Mobi seat change sits behind a flag, which lowers the risk to art he already approved. Acceptance is numeric for every item (offPx === 0 gate rows, a perf budget table, the 1300 ms loader filmstrip).
scores.weaknesses:
1. Lifting the hero out of page.js:172-245 into a new HomeHero.jsx is the riskiest refactor here, because it touches the state-aware CTAs (L-006..L-009) and the recovery branch.
2. Turning the pointer spotlight into a gaze that follows the pointer on desktop and the last touch on phones is a new per-input feature. It adds pointermove work and runs against its own '0 rAF idle' claim.
3. The room is 520x600 on desktop and 358x268 in the phone's first viewport, so it becomes the LCP element and must load eagerly at high priority. At the 2x density a phone uses, the 40 KB AVIF budget is doubtful.
4. Its targets are the most aggressive (LCP ≤2.2 s, TBT ≤250 ms, 0 frames over 100 ms). They are unlikely to be proven in one night; at best they are a goal.
5. One cell in the Night table is unresolved ('2 px left tick? No: ...'), which is a spec ambiguity for the engineer.
6. The exam stacks two switches (Question/Review and MockMob/NTA), which is extra state to build and test.
7. Its own risk note says 'second guesses' may rest on Pro-only data, an unverified truth claim.
8. The tap still fills one painted sheet bubble per tap and keeps the buzz, so part of LK67's 'tap feels weird' survives.
9. Erase-then-type is the Preparoo grammar (R-054).
scores.ruleBreaks: None hard. Two soft points need the owner: the static-H1 ruling of 1 Nov is reversed (flagged), and the statement scrub becomes steps on desktop too, which he could read as a removed animation (L-005). 'Second guesses' must be checked against the capability gates before it ships.

scores.strengths: It has the best verification plan. P6 is a dedicated gate packet (home-1104-gate.mjs, landing_L_checklist.test.mjs, a section inventory diffed against main) built in parallel and run last, so every acceptance check is a named, runnable check. The exam is rebuilt inside ExamComparator.jsx under the same export, so page.js does not change for it. That is the lowest merge risk of the three exam plans, and examPreviewParity.test.mjs stops the preview drifting from TestPageClient strings. It keeps the baked seat poses, so there is no new art pipeline tonight. The loader runs on first visit only and is skipped for signed-in users and hashes. The statement is one 3-step path at both widths. The typed subjects are the safest truth claim (a test checks them against CUET_PUBLIC_ALLOWED_SUBJECTS). The 'mm:jump' contract and the scrollGesture.mjs pure decideStep unit tests make the scroll packet testable without a browser.

scores.strengths: It is the deepest and most precise spec, with file:line removals, token tables and per-item acceptance with tests named (night_calm_1104.test.mjs greps volt outside allowed selectors, oneGesture.test.mjs, examScreen.test.mjs, landingMobi.test.mjs). Its performance thinking is the best: the rig idles in CSS, the room sits lazy below the key so the server-rendered h1 is the LCP on phones, PipGuide caches its stations, fitAll leaves the scroll frame, and steps toggle attributes without React. The bubble changes only on sample state, never on taps, which addresses LK67 most cleanly. The opening layer ends at visibility:hidden in CSS, so it cannot become a stuck layer. The server text and the resting text are the approved sentence. It enforces one volt key per viewport.
scores.weaknesses:
1. A defect I measured in its own mock-up: at 44 px 'Every mark traced.' is 386 px and the resting 'Know what to fix.' is 352 px in a 350 px column at 390. Even 'Fresh every time.' is exactly 350. At 360 (a 320 px column) every phrase overflows by 30-66 px. Its claim that '≤18 characters fits 358 px' is false, and the h1 must drop to about 39 px, which breaks its own 1.46x type ladder.
2. The loader runs on every new session ('short', 1.28 s), so most student visits get a full-screen curtain. That is the highest perceived-slowness risk on cold 4G.
3. It has the largest scope for one night: a new pose generator, all seven baked seat poses retired (changes approved art, with no flag), a BrandIcon rail, Literata preloaded on /, Geist Mono removed, the nav CTA changed on IntersectionObserver, a split statement (4 steps on phones, scrub plus settle on desktop, two code paths to gate), and a new ExamScreen file.
4. P2 owns page.js and has to integrate P3 and P5, so it is a bottleneck that lands last.
5. Literata adds 52 KB on the LCP path.
6. Its own mock-up wordmark has no volt dot in the bar or in either loader frame, while clarity and feel both draw it.
scores.ruleBreaks: The logo is shown without its small volt dot (the owner said to keep logo B with the dot). The typed headline overflows its column at 390 and 360 as specified. Retiring the approved photo-real seat poses without a flag risks his 'Mobi is good' verdict.

best: feel. It is the most buildable and least regression-prone base. Its typed slot fits at 360 (I measured 313 px in a 320 px column). Its loader runs on first visit only, any input skips it, and it holds the fewest visits behind a curtain. The rig idles at 0 rAF. The statement is one step path at both widths, and the seat-pose change sits behind a flag. Six packets with a stated merge order fit 4-6 engineers in one night. Before building, the spec must (a) drop the gaze feature or limit it to desktop pointer on one compositor transform, (b) settle the Night table cell, (c) prove 'second guesses' against the capability gates or swap the phrase, and (d) decide the room's LCP: eager, a measured byte budget, and fixed dimensions.
graft: Clarity's P6 gate packet: scripts/design-audit/home-1104-gate.mjs plus data/tests/landing_L_checklist.test.mjs (one test id or named screenshot per L-001..L-045) and a section-inventory diff against main. It is built in parallel and runs on localhost and then production.

Clarity's exam plan: rebuild in place inside ExamComparator.jsx under the same export and #exam-experience id, so page.js is untouched. Add examPreviewParity.test.mjs, which asserts that every runner string shown exists in TestPageClient.jsx.

Clarity's pure scrollGesture.mjs decideStep({dy, dt, vEnd, locked, atEdge}), unit-tested for every bench row, alongside the real-Chrome CDP gate. It is fast to run and catches regressions without a browser.

Clarity's truth test for typed content: a test checks every typed phrase against its capability source, as clarity checks CUET_PUBLIC_ALLOWED_SUBJECTS. Applied to feel's three phrases, it would settle 'second guesses'.
Brand's sample-state bubble rules (load, right, miss, after five; at most 44 characters; never changed by a tap). They make the 'no bubble change on tap' acceptance a CDP-tap test.
Brand's night_calm grep test: fail on rgba(210,240,0 or #d2f000 outside the allowed selectors, and on volt radial-gradients, coloured blurred box-shadows and backdrop-filter on content.

Brand's server-rendered resting text plus a visually hidden full sentence and an aria-hidden slot with a sizer. Add a Playwright check that every phrase and the sizer fit the column at 360, 375, 390 and 412, with scrollWidth equal to innerWidth.

Brand's opening safety: the run gate wraps every storage access in try/catch with a safe fallback, the layer ends on visibility:hidden with fill-mode forwards, and elementFromPoint at the key's centre returns the key by 1.5 s.
Brand's 'one volt key per viewport' check, but done statically (the bar key always secondary, as feel already does) rather than swapped on IntersectionObserver.
Brand's step-driven visuals via data-step attributes with no React re-render per step, and the 'no non-passive listener when no story is near' assertion (it protects LK47).
Clarity's 'mm:jump' event contract for programmatic jumps (goTo, HashSettle, DemoJump, nav and position-band links) so a jump from outside the story is not clamped at the first rest.
mustAvoid: A typed phrase or sizer wider than its column at any phone width. I measured brand's 'Every mark traced.' at 386 px in a 350 px column and clarity's 'Business Studies' sizer causing 17 px of sideways scroll at 360. Fit tests at 360-412 must gate this.
A loader that runs on every new session, or one that ignores input. First visit only, any input skips it, and skip it on hash, same-origin referrer and reduced motion.
Any per-pointermove or per-touch rAF work on phones (feel's gaze on 'last touch'), and any always-on non-passive touchmove or wheel listener. Register them only while a story is within one screen.
A statement that steps on phones but scrubs on desktop. Keep one code path, or the gesture gate must cover both.
More than one packet editing page.js. One integration owner lands last, and the others export components with stable props and the data-step contract.

Deleting heroLines.test, scrollStorySpeed.test or the release9 grid/dots assertion. Rewrite each deliberately, record the owner's 4 Nov words verbatim against L-016 and L-043, and keep a failing-first test for one gesture = one step.

Gesture tests in chrome-headless-shell, which never scrolls on synthetic input. Use real Chrome with timestamped CDP touch and wheel, then a real iPhone, a real Android and his own phone before shipping.

Changing the .mm Day and Night tokens without a Day and Night screenshot pass of every public page (pricing, the /cuet pages, signup, the DU tools) and a contrast check of du.css's roughly 20 hand-tuned Night overrides.
Shipping or showing the logo without its small volt dot (brand's mock-up omits it).
Replacing the approved baked seat poses without a flag and his look.
A new accent hue (clarity's #cddd5a). 'CUET 2027' stays the logo volt at Night and #526700 in Day (L-017).

An LCP image in the first viewport that is lazy or unbudgeted. Either keep the room below the key and lazy, so the h1 is the LCP, or make it eager with fixed dimensions and a measured byte budget at 2x density for the active theme only.
Reporting performance targets as achieved without a real-Chrome 4x-CPU run on localhost and then production. Lab numbers are a diagnosis, not a claim.
Truth claims in typed phrases or facts that rest on Pro-only data shown as free ('second guesses'), and 'never repeats' wording (L-041).
Removing tap acts, the buzz, the theme-toggle motion or any section or story while 'simplifying'. Convert them and log each conversion.
